claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for your help. I'm inquiring about my child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your child, Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some details about your circumstances.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful information.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for clarifying that.

**Are you responsible for financially supporting Alex?** (In other words, do you provide for his day-to-day care and maintenance?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I provide for all of Alex's day-to-day needs - everything from food and clothing to school things and everything else he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's very helpful.

**What is your residency status in the UK?** (For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another type of visa or immigration status?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen and I live here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that clarification.

**Are you currently receiving any income-related benefits?** (Such as Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Is Alex in full-time education, apprenticeship, or training?** (Child Benefit can usually be paid until age 16, or until age 19 if the child is in approved education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's only 12, so he's just in regular school - year 8 at the local secondary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that.

**Has Alex been in hospital or local authority care at any point, or does he currently live away from home for any reason?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's always lived at home with me and hasn't been in hospital or care or anything.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the eligibility rules to provide you with an accurate outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Excellent news!** You are **eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

You meet all the eligibility criteria:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- You live with Alex and are responsible for his day-to-day care and maintenance
- You are a British citizen and UK resident
- There are no restrictions affecting your eligibility

You can proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex. If you have any further questions or need assistance with the application process, please feel free to ask!
